==English== {{wp|}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|horse-hoarse}} :* {{IPA|en|/fɔːs/|a=RP}} :* {{IPA|en|/foːs/|a=SSB,AU,NZ}} :* {{enPR|fôrs|a=GenAm,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/foɹs/|[fo̞ɹs]}} :** {{audio|en|en-us-force.ogg|a=US}} * {{enPR|fōrs|a=non-horse-hoarse}} :* {{IPA|en|/foɾs/|a=Scotland}} :* {{IPA|en|/fɔːs/|a=Manchester}} :* {{IPA|en|/foəs/|a=Eastern New England}} :* {{IPA|en|/fɔəs/|a=19th century <>,obsolete}} :* {{IPA|en|/foːɹs/|a=early 20th century <>,rhotic,near-obsolete}} :* {{IPA|en|/foː(ɾ)s/|/fɒ(ɾ)s/|a=South Asia|q2=spelling pronunciation}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)s|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰerǵʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|force}}, {{m|enm|fors}}, {{m|enm|forse}}, from {{der|en|fro|force}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|fortia}}, a noun derived from the neuter plural of {{der|en|la|fortis|t=strong}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰerǵʰ-|t=to rise, high, hill}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{cap|ability}} to influence; [[strength]] or [[energy]] of [[body]] or [[mind]]; [[active]] [[power]]; [[vigour]]; [[might]]; [[capacity]] of [[exercise|exercising]] an [[influence]] or [[produce|producing]] an [[effect]]. #: {{ux|en|the '''force''' of an appeal, an argument, or a contract}} #: {{ux|en|[[show of '''force''']]}} #* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=14|passage=He was, in the full '''force''' of the words, a good man.}} #* {{quote-av|en|author=Drachinifel|title= Anti-Slavery Patrols - The West Africa Squadron|date=1 December 2018|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TiSekII0sjw|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20241129115918/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TiSekII0sjw|archivedate=29 November 2024|accessdate=4 January 2025|time=9:45|text=After his actions were challenged by foreign governments and Parliament initially tried to put a stop to his action, Denman returned home and argued his case with enough '''force''' that, by 1848, the Royal Navy was handed active permission and ''encouragement'' to raze every last slave factory they could find to the ground, and ''full'' authority to stop ''any'' ship, of ''any'' flag, that was thought to be a slaver, with a guarantee with{{sic}} ''no'' censure from the government.}} # {{senseid|en|Q11402}} {{lb|en|physics}} A [[physical]] [[quantity]] that denotes ability to [[push]], [[pull]], [[twist]] or [[accelerate]] a body and which has a [[direction]] and is measured in a unit dimensioned in [[mass]] × [[distance]]/[[time]]² (ML/T²): [[SI]]: [[newton]] (N); [[CGS]]: [[dyne]] (dyn). #: {{cot|en|moment of force|torque|work|energy|power}} ## {{lb|en|uncountable}} The generalized abstraction of this concept. ##: {{ux|en|{{cap|torque}} is the rotational version of force.}} ##: {{ux|en|Force is the result of fundamental interactions.}} ## {{lb|en|countable}} A particular form or type of force. ##: {{ux|en|Most physicists deem there to be four [[fundamental force]]s: the [[weak force]], the [[strong force]], [[gravitation]], and the [[electromagnetic force]].}} ##: {{ux|en|[[fictitious force]]s}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Searching for the Secrets of Gravity|author=John Boslough|page=563 |text=As the '''force''' that attracts conglomerates of matter to one another, gravity has a limitless pull.}} ### {{lb|en|humorous|or|science fiction|with {{m|en|the}}|often|capitalized}}{{C|en|Star Wars}} A [[metaphysical]] and [[ubiquitous]] power from the fictional ''{{w|Star Wars}}'' universe created by {{w|George Lucas}}. {{n-g|See usage note.}} {{defdate|1977}} ###* {{RQ:Guardian|date=1999-09-28|author=Mike Selvey|title=Crenshaw vindicated by a chain reaction|url=https://www.theguardian.com/ryder/Story/0,,202335,00.html|passage=The Europeans tried, my goodness how they tried. But on the day the US proved too strong and too inspired. They were, dammit, just better. And when Leonard's putt dropped they clearly had the '''force''' with them as well.}} ###* {{quote-av|en|actor=w:Ian McDiarmid|role=w:Palpatine|title={{w|Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith}}|writer=w:George Lucas|year=2005|year_published=2005|text=The dark side of the '''Force''' is a pathway to many abilities some consider to be unnatural.}} ## {{lb|en|countable}} An instance of a physical force. ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012-03|author=w:Henry Petroski| volume=100| issue=2| page=112–3| magazine=w:American Scientist| title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/opening-doors Opening Doors]| passage=A doorknob of whatever roundish shape is effectively a continuum of levers, with the axis of the latching mechanism—known as the spindle—being the fulcrum about which the turning takes place. Applying a '''force''' tangential to the knob is essentially equivalent to applying one perpendicular to a radial line defining the lever.}} ##: {{ux|en|Two forces acting upon the same point on an object will cancel out only if they have equal magnitude and opposite directions.}} ## {{lb|en|mass noun|possibly proscribed}} Force understood as something of which there can be an amount. ##: {{ux|en|Heavier objects are those that are subject to more gravitational force.}} # {{lb|en|countable}} Anything that is able to make a [[substantial]] [[change]] in a [[person]] or [[thing]]. # Something or anything that has the power to produce a physical effect upon something else, such as causing it to move or change shape. # {{lb|en|countable}} Something that exerts influence. #: {{near-syn|en|influence|factor|pressure}} #: {{ux|en|[[force of nature]]}} ## {{lb|en|when in reference to that which it affects}} Something that, over time, influences a system with which it interacts (''with a connotation of [[underlying]]ness, subtlety, or indirectness''). ##: {{ux|en|I believe that the main long-term force that guides a society's evolution is not the economy or the leaders, but the culture.}} ##: {{ux|en|Some skeptics have attributed changing temperatures to forces out of our control, such as axial procession.}} ##: {{ux|en|[[market force]]s}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} {{cap|power}} [[exert]]ed against [[will]] or [[consent]]; [[compulsory]] power; [[violence]]; [[coercion]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|text=which now they hold by '''force''', and not by right}} ## {{lb|en|legal}} Either [[unlawful]] violence, as in a "'''forced entry'''", or lawful [[compulsion]]. # {{lb|en|countable}} A group organized for the goal of [[attack]]ing, [[control]]ling, or [[constrain]]ing, especially one with a set command structure (in particular, a military or police group). #: {{ux|en|[[air force]]; [[police '''force''']]}} #: {{ux|en|Force Z}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Cymbeline|text=Is Lucius general of the '''forces'''?}} #* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|text="A fine man, that Dunwody, yonder," commented the young captain, as they parted, and as he turned to his prisoner. "We'll see him on in Washington some day. He is strengthening his '''forces''' now against Mr. Benton out there.{{nb...}}."}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=April 15, 2004|work=The Scotsman |title=[http://www.scotsman.com/news/morning_swoop_in_hunt_for_jodi_s_killer_1_521912 Morning swoop in hunt for Jodi's killer] |passage=For Lothian and Borders Police, the early-morning raid had come at the end one of biggest investigations carried out by the '''force''', which had originally presented a dossier of evidence on the murder of Jodi Jones to the Edinburgh procurator-fiscal, William Gallagher, on 25 November last year.}} ## Any large, organized group involved in a military [[engagement]]. ## {{lb|en|in the singular or plural}} Military {{cap|[[personnel]]}}, collectively, including any vehicles, ships, or aircraft. More broadly, the [[military]] or [[police]] altogether. ##: {{ux|en|After only a week, Japanese forces had captured Singapore from the British.}} ##: {{ux|en|reinforcements grew the American '''force''' in the area to 9,000}} ##: {{ux|en|Roman forces were}} ### {{lb|en|usually with "the"|in the singular or plural}} {{synonym of|en|police force}}. ###* {{quote-book|en|year=1880|title=[U.S.] House documents|page=64 |text=Q. All the time that he was on the '''force'''?
A. I cannot say that; but there were men on with me when I was on the '''force''' who were very good Republicans.
Q. During all this time you have been on the police force?}} ###* '''1992''', {{w|Rage Against the Machine}} (band), ''{{w|Killing in the Name}}'': ###* {{quote-book|en|date=2012-02-01|author=Janice Kay Johnson|title=Between Love and Duty|publisher=Harlequin|isbn=9781459221086|page=77 |text=Niall was on the '''force''', too, a detective in major crimes.}} # {{lb|en|legal|uncountable}} The state of having legal [[weight]], of being legally [[valid]],. #: {{near-syn|en|effect}} #: {{ux|en|The law will [[come into force|come into '''force''']] in January.}} # {{lb|en|countable}} A [[magic]] [[trick]] in which the outcome is known to the magician beforehand, especially one involving the apparent free choice of a card by another person. # {{lb|en|linguistics|semantics|pragmatics}} Ability of an [[utterance]] or its element (word, form, [[prosody]], ...) to [[effect#Verb|effect]] a given meaning. # {{lb|en|financial mathematics|actuarial science}} The [[annualized]] [[instantaneous]] [[rate of change]] at a particular [[timepoint]]. #: {{ux|en|{{w|force of mortality}}}} =====Usage notes===== * {{sense|science fiction}} Outside of fiction, ''the force'' may be used as an alternative to invoking {{m|en|luck}}, {{m|en|destiny}}{{,}} or {{m|en|God}}. For example, ''the force was with him'' instead of ''luck was on his side'', or ''may the force be with you'' instead of ''may God be with you''. =====Sense overview===== Most of the main senses can be placed under the following umbrellas, all centered on the notion of [[influence]]: * The ability to exert influence; in other words, [[power]] or [[strength]] (the original sense borrowed from French). * Influence itself. * Something by which influence takes place (as in the physics senses). * Something that can or does exert influence (as in the military senses). * Forced influence, i.e. [[coercion]]. =====Hyponyms===== {{col4|en|air force |armed forces,armed force |breakout force|land force |brute force|legal force |centrifugal force |centripetal force |conservative force |Coriolis
